body.statement: For the threshold sequence \(\varepsilon_n=3\sqrt{\mu^\star\log(n)/n}\), with \(p,k,L,B,\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max}\) fixed, \[\sup_{\substack{\|\beta\|_2\le B,\;\sigma\in[\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max}]\\ \text{admissible conditional-noise laws}}}\left|\frac{R_n(\beta,\sigma,\varepsilon_n)}{\sigma^2\Phi^\star/n}-1\right|\longrightarrow0.\]
body.justification: This establishes that the exact population \(A\)-risk is attained uniformly over the stated fixed-dimensional coefficient and noise class.
body.gap: PFED gives near-optimal passive-risk control, whereas this statement isolates the all-order limited-supply oracle constant and its exact leverage-dependent threshold.
body.consumer: The result justifies replacing numerical population design search by the uniform dosage in sufficiently large independent-delivery screens.
body.proof_tex:
By \(\textnormal{ass:fixed-dimension}\), the quantities \(q\), \(\mu^\star\), and \(\Phi^\star\) are fixed as \(n\to\infty\); moreover, the definitions of the leverage and criterion give \(0<\mu^\star<\infty\) and \(0<\Phi^\star<\infty\). Since \(n/\log n\to\infty\), for all sufficiently large \(n\) one has \(n>36\mu^\star\log n\). Thus \(\textnormal{def:oracle-threshold}\) applies and gives
\[
 \varepsilon_n=3\sqrt{\frac{\mu^\star\log n}{n}},
 \qquad
 0<\varepsilon_n<\frac12,
 \qquad
 \varepsilon_n\longrightarrow0.
\]
Indeed, the middle inequality is equivalent to \(n>36\mu^\star\log n\).

Write \(b_n=b_{n,\varepsilon_n}\). The concentration conclusion in \(\textnormal{thm:risk-sandwich}\), followed by the definition of \(\varepsilon_n\), yields
\[
 b_n
 \le 2q\exp\!\left\{-\frac{n\varepsilon_n^2}{3\mu^\star}\right\}
 =2q\exp\{-3\log n\}
 =2qn^{-3}.
\tag{1}
\]
For every coefficient vector, noise scale, and conditional-noise law in the supremum of the theorem, define
\[
 \rho_n(\beta,\sigma)
 =\frac{R_n(\beta,\sigma,\varepsilon_n)}{\sigma^2\Phi^\star/n}.
\]
This ratio is well defined because \(\sigma\ge\sigma_{\min}>0\) by the variance-range condition used in \(\textnormal{thm:risk-sandwich}\), and \(\Phi^\star>0\). Dividing the two-sided conclusion of \(\textnormal{thm:risk-sandwich}\) by \(\sigma^2\Phi^\star/n\) gives
\[
 \frac{1-b_n}{1+\varepsilon_n}
 \le \rho_n(\beta,\sigma)
 \le \frac{1}{1-\varepsilon_n}
   +\frac{nB^2b_n}{\sigma^2\Phi^\star}.
\tag{2}
\]
The deficit of the left endpoint in \((2)\) from one satisfies
\[
 1-\frac{1-b_n}{1+\varepsilon_n}
 =\frac{\varepsilon_n+b_n}{1+\varepsilon_n}
 \le \varepsilon_n+b_n,
\tag{3}
\]
whereas, because \(0<\varepsilon_n<1/2\), the excess of the right endpoint over one satisfies
\[
 \frac{1}{1-\varepsilon_n}-1
   +\frac{nB^2b_n}{\sigma^2\Phi^\star}
 =\frac{\varepsilon_n}{1-\varepsilon_n}
   +\frac{nB^2b_n}{\sigma^2\Phi^\star}
 \le 2\varepsilon_n
   +\frac{nB^2b_n}{\sigma^2\Phi^\star}.
\tag{4}
\]
Equations \((2)\)--\((4)\), the bound \(\sigma^2\ge\sigma_{\min}^2\), and \((1)\) therefore imply, simultaneously for every element of the stated parameter and conditional-noise class,
\[
 \left|\rho_n(\beta,\sigma)-1\right|
 \le
 2\varepsilon_n+2qn^{-3}
 +\frac{2B^2q}{\sigma_{\min}^2\Phi^\star}n^{-2}.
\tag{5}
\]
The right-hand side of \((5)\) is deterministic, does not depend on \(\beta\), \(\sigma\), or the admissible conditional-noise law, and converges to zero because \(\varepsilon_n\to0\) while all displayed constants are fixed. Taking the required supremum in \((5)\) proves the asserted uniform convergence. The argument fixes \(p,k,L,B,\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max}\), so it entails neither growing-dimensional nor vanishing-supply uniformity.
